Final categorization: OK  
(Justification: The paper presents original research with a primary focus on simulating and assessing spatial uncertainties in future agricultural land use allocation across Europe (EU27), which constitutes a national-scale spatial implementation covering multiple countries in their entirety. It explicitly implements two contrasting, quantitatively specified future scenarios (Marketeer and Musketeer) derived from SRES storylines and compares them systematically. The study uses a coupled modeling framework (LEITAP + Dyna-CLUE) to produce 1×1 km spatially explicit LULC projections for arable land and pasture, including mapped outputs of occurrence probabilities and transition likelihoods (abandonment/expansion). Quantitative metrics are reported, including mean and standard deviation of land use change rates, confidence intervals, and probabilistic spatial measures based on 50 model runs per scenario. All core inclusion criteria are met, and none of the exclusion criteria apply—the analysis is not global-only (it disaggregates to national and sub-national levels), includes explicit LULC prediction, is not species/ecological/bioenergy-focused, and goes beyond single-scenario or qualitative approaches.)
